import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 63

Let $A$ be the smallest set containing $2$ and $3$ and such that $a_1a_2 - 1 \in A$
if $a_1, a_2 \in A$. Does $A$ have positive density?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
- [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»`.
-/

findings.description: The forwarding text silently identifies two different generating rules. Lines 23–24, following Green’s displayed Problem 63, allow equal inputs in a₁a₂ − 1. However, the imported `Erdos424.nextGeneration` requires `x ≠ y`. In `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` I proved that `8 ∉ Erdos424.generatedSet`, whereas any set containing 3 and closed under the unrestricted rule contains 8 = 3·3 − 1. This is a source ambiguity rather than a confirmed misformalization: Erdős’s original paper explicitly requires distinct elements, and Green himself identifies the problem with Erdős 424 and OEIS A005244. The imported definition faithfully follows that primary reference. The difference between the sets alone does not establish inequivalence of their positive-density questions.
findings.source_evidence: Green, https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf, Problem 63, pp. 30–31: “Let A be the smallest set containing 2 and 3 and such that a₁a₂ − 1 ∈ A if a₁, a₂ ∈ A.” His comments identify A005244 and Erdős 424. In contrast, Erdős, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory III (1977), p. 71, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf, says: “Form all products of two distinct elements of the sequence, subtract 1 and append these elements to the sequence.” The OEIS b-file begins 2, 3, 5, 9, 14, consistent with distinct inputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that this module forwards to the distinct-input Erdős/Hofstadter formulation, noting the omitted distinctness condition in Green’s displayed wording. If the intention is to formalize Green’s literal unrestricted rule as well, add a separately identified unrestricted-input variant, or document an equivalence of the density questions. Do not simply remove `x ≠ y` from the canonical Erdős definition, which matches the primary reference.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/ — identifies the problem list as updated January 2026.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliography used to locate Green’s primary reference.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf — P. Erdős, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory III, especially p. 71.

https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-34.pdf; https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-33.pdf; https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-28.pdf — inspected while resolving incorrect bibliography links; not used as evidence for the finding.
Crossref bibliographic query for Problems and results on combinatorial number theory III — confirmed DOI 10.1007/BFb0063064.
could_not_verify: file — I did not establish whether the positive-density question for Green’s literal unrestricted generating rule is equivalent to the imported distinct-input question. This is why the forwarding discrepancy is flagged only as questionable, not as a proven mathematical misformalization.
review.notes: The reviewed file contains only imports and a module docstring: it introduces no definitions, theorems, answer slots, or status annotations. The finding concerns its forwarding description, not an independently stated theorem. I inspected the canonical module and density definitions, and successfully compiled scratch proofs checking the first generations, empty/singleton inputs, exclusion of 8, the lower bound 2 on generated elements, closure and minimality for distinct inputs, and the finite counting ratios used for density. No additional mathematical defect was identified. Green’s current PDF still presents the question as open. The Erdős 424 webpage and full OEIS entry returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; their latest commentary and status could not be checked. No stale-status claim is made.
